title: The Mirror Clause of the Geometric Selection Conjecture Is Empty: note, source and check
description:
Note, LaTeX source and check for The Mirror Clause of the Geometric Selection Conjecture Is Empty by Deep Bhattacharjee and Ushashi Bhattacharya.

The Geometric Selection Conjecture asks for a functional on the heterotic landscape, built from the Weil-Petersson metric and invariant under mirror symmetry, whose unique minimum is a phenomenologically viable vacuum. The paper on the Dwork quintic (hexagonmath.org 2610.00446v1) showed that the conjecture holds if and only if there is a viable vacuum fixed by the mirror involution wherever it is defined. The note proves that the fixed-point clause is never satisfied: a vacuum fixed by the mirror involution has a threefold isomorphic to its own mirror, hence equal Hodge numbers, vanishing Euler number and, on its component of the landscape, a bundle with c_3 = 0; by Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch it has zero net families and violates the three-family condition. Consequently no vacuum built on the tangent bundle of any Calabi-Yau threefold, or on a deformation of it, is ever selected, and the conjecture is equivalent to the existence of one viable vacuum on a component of the landscape carrying no standard embedding, with no condition involving mirror symmetry; the same holds for invariance under any compact group of isometries containing the mirror involution. The existence statement itself remains open.

The archive holds the compiled note, its source as one zip, and a Python check of the lemma and the corollary on the Hodge data of self-mirror and three-family threefolds (514 checks).
